# Proposed ECON101 preparation guidance

Proposal only; active guidance is unchanged. Human review and deliberate activation are separate.

## Course overview

This synthetic course develops marginal decision analysis and causal experiment design. Week 03 connects incremental contribution, sunk costs, random assignment and uncertainty. Preparation should compare feasible alternatives and identify evidence that could change the decision, not present scenario assumptions as observations. `ECON101/Syllabus.md`

## Brief structure

1. Overview
2. Reading synthesis
3. Key concepts
4. Preparation questions
5. Discussion points
6. Sources

Use these six syllabus-specified sections for class preparation. Synthesize both assigned readings; distinguish their claims, practical applications and limitations. Answer supplied preparation questions rather than inventing questions attributed to the instructor. Bring discussion points about evidence that could overturn a recommendation. Cite the exact supplied material paths in Sources. `ECON101/Syllabus.md`

## Evidence and quantitative work

Separate stated assumptions, supplied observations and conditional conclusions. When deriving quantitative values, execute the arithmetic and report inputs, assumptions and results; check inputs against the supplied materials. Flag missing data instead of inventing demand effects or tested outcomes. A positive scenario result is not an observed business success. `ECON101/Syllabus.md` `ECON101/guidance/prep-guidance.md`

## Policy and scope

The supplied invented syllabus and active guidance explicitly permit AI assistance for prep, full drafts, discussion and review in this fixture only. They do not authorize submission. This proposal neither creates course permission nor authenticates an instructor; confirm applicable policy separately before using it for real coursework. Use only supplied fixture sources. Assignment-specific scope and output rules remain authoritative for assignment work; this prep format must not replace them. `ECON101/Syllabus.md` `ECON101/guidance/prep-guidance.md`

## Open questions

Grading weights, attendance requirements and exam rules are unspecified. The sources supply no student voice preferences or empirical pilot outcomes. Preserve these as unknown; request authoritative information when needed. Review this proposal against current course rules before any manual activation. `ECON101/Syllabus.md`
